stances.claim: FVR -- though told by CJ that CJ neither campaigned nor voted for him -- still offered CJ the DOJ secretariat, then the Supreme Court seat after the DOJ offer was respectfully declined, and once on the Court never spoke or influenced CJ in any manner, fully respecting CJ's independence even when CJ voted against FVR's known political wishes; a 'gentleman-patriot.'

stances.claim: FLP, in partnership with the Tan Yan Kee Foundation, will grant P200,000 each to 21 law-school scholars (10 fourth-year, 11 third-year); honor the three Exemplary 2022 bar topnotchers at P100,000 each; and recognize Latin-honors graduates at P25,000-P100,000 each.

FLP, in partnership with the Ayala Corporation, will award dissertation winners (First P320,000; Second P220,000; three Third Prizes P120,000; five finalists P20,000) plus cash gifts to faculty advisers (P100,000, P75,000, P50,000).

FLP, starting this year in partnership with the Metro Pacific Investments Foundation, will award five P450,000 'Esmel' fellowships to MBA-track students concentrating in entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics, or business law.

FLP's first decade (2011-2021) concentrated on its liberty programs; its second decade (2021-2031) will add the prosperity side -- culminating in the Center for Liberty and Prosperity with an interactive Museum (in partnership with the SC) for liberty, and a P1B+ 'Entrepreneurship Fund' for MSMEs with active Esmel-fellow assistance for prosperity.

The 'gentleman-patriot' epithet for FVR -- quietly setting up the C45 institutional-memoir follow-up.

Comprehensive name-by-name enumeration of every scholar, winner, and fellow with their respective schools -- turning the column into a permanent FLP record while also serving as a recruitment beacon for the next cycle.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with a candid disclosure: although CJ told FVR he 'did not campaign or vote for him,' the late President still offered him the DOJ secretariat on June 17, 1992 -- and when CJ respectfully declined, changed the offer to a seat on the Supreme Court, then 'never spoke or influenced me, in any manner, in the discharge of my duties' -- a 'gentleman-patriot' (with more on him promised in another column). The column then turns to the Aug 11 FLP awarding event with CJ Alexander G. Gesmundo as guest of honor. In partnership with the Tan Yan Kee Foundation, FLP grants P200,000 each to 21 law-school scholars (10 fourth-year and 11 third-year, named individually by school -- FEU, St Louis U, UP, UCebu, UST, UCordilleras, DLSU, DLS-Lipa); also honored are the three Exemplary 2022 bar topnotchers (Domingo, Mata, Omamalin) at P100,000 each, with Latin-honors graduates receiving P25,000-P100,000 each. In partnership with the Ayala Corporation, the dissertation writing contest awards range from P320,000 (Patricia Anne Alarios, AdMU) down to P20,000 (five finalists), with faculty advisers receiving P50,000-P100,000. Starting this year, in a new partnership with the Metro Pacific Investments Foundation, FLP will also award five P450,000 'Esmel' fellowships to MBA-track students in entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics, or business law. The strategic announcement: FLP's first decade (2011-2021) concentrated on its liberty programs; its second decade (2021-2031) will add the prosperity side. Its ultimate liberty project is the Center for Liberty and Prosperity, hosting an interactive Museum in partnership with the Supreme Court; its ultimate prosperity project is a P1B+ 'Entrepreneurship Fund' for micro, small, and medium enterprises, with the active assistance of its Esmel fellows.
